title: La Pasarela de la Moda
subtitle: Relearn and practise all of Unit 7 — clothes, este/ese/aquel, ponerse, llevar, colours and shop talk — and walk the runway.
module: Unit 7: La Moda y las Compras (Fashion & Shopping)

learningFocus.summary: This activity lets true beginners relearn and practise the whole of Pre-IG Stage 1 Spanish Unit 7 — Clothing, Shopping & Style — through six scaffolded levels. Students label real clothing in a photograph and learn each item with its article (el/la/los/las), compare Spain and Latin America vocabulary (el jersey/el suéter, las gafas/los lentes), choose the three-distance demonstratives este/ese/aquel with the right gender and number, dress a mannequin by building reflexive sentences with ponerse (me pongo, te pones, se pone, nos ponemos, os ponéis, se ponen), describe outfits with llevar, indefinite articles and colour adjectives that follow the noun and agree with it (una camiseta blanca, unos zapatos negros), and rebuild a real shop dialogue about prices and sizes. A final level connects the language to culture — Zara's fast fashion versus Guatemalan backstrap-loom weaving — and a short reading in Spanish. Every level moves from recognising to producing the language, with instant feedback that names the exact part of the sentence to fix.

orient.objective: Use Spanish clothing words, este/ese/aquel, ponerse and llevar to describe, wear and buy clothes in simple Spanish sentences.
orient.courseLink: This activity revises all of Unit 7 (Clothing & Shopping) in Pre-IG Stage 1 Spanish and prepares the verbs and describing words you will use in Unit 8: Holidays & Travel.
orient.mission: Fashion Week starts today and you are the star stylist. Pass six levels — from naming clothes to walking the runway — and earn your way from Aprendiz to Icono de la Moda. Everything is in easy Spanish, and every instruction is in English.
steps: Meet the three rules of Unit 7 below (tap the cards).
Choose your best guess for the Hypothesis question.
Play the six levels: El Armario, Señala, Vístete, Pasarela, En la Tienda, Cultura.
Check your Record, then write your Explain and Apply answers.
Finish the Knowledge Check and generate your Learning Evidence.
successCriteria: You will be able to name at least 8 clothing items with the correct article (el, la, los, las).
You will be able to say this/that/that over there (este, ese, aquel) with the correct gender and number.
You will be able to use me pongo / lleva and a colour word to say what someone wears.
You will be able to follow and rebuild a simple conversation in a clothes shop.
orient.realLife: Next time you shop on holiday in Spain or Latin America, you will point at a jacket across the shop and ask “¿Cuánto cuesta aquella chaqueta?” — and the shop assistant will understand you.

predict.prompt: You are in a shop. The red shirt (la camisa) is on a shelf far away from both you and the assistant. What do you think you say?
predict.hint: Remember: Spanish has three distances, and “camisa” is a feminine word.

investigate.title: La Pasarela de la Moda
investigate.lede: Six levels, one fashion week. In each level, pick the Spanish that fits — you get a second chance if you slip, and a clear hint showing what to fix. Earn XP, build a streak and climb the ranks.

record.intro: Every answer you gave is logged here automatically — your own practice record. Look for the words you got wrong first time.
record.emptyText: No answers yet. Play the levels in the interactive above.

explain.prompt: Look at your Record and choose ONE answer you got wrong or needed two tries for. Write the Spanish words from that task, explain the rule in English (for example: why the ending changes, or which pronoun goes with which person), and write one correct Spanish example of your own.
explain.lede: Quote a real task from your own Record — not a general rule from memory.
explain.skillFocus: Use your own practice record to explain a Spanish rule clearly, with a correct example.

apply.prompt: A friend asks what you are wearing for a school party. Write 3 short Spanish sentences: (1) say what you or a friend is wearing using the verb llevar with two items and their colours; (2) say what you put on first using ponerse; (3) ask a shop assistant the price of a jacket that is far away from you. Then add one line in English saying who the sentences are about.
apply.lede: Use real Unit 7 words. Colours go after the noun, and the shop question needs the correct word for “that over there”.
apply.skillFocus: Use Unit 7 Spanish in a new, real-life situation with correct endings and word order.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: You point at the sunglasses (las gafas) on a shelf far away from you. Which is correct?
knowledgeCheck.explain: Far away means aquel-. “Las gafas” is feminine and plural, so the form is aquellas.
“Nosotros” (we) goes with the pronoun nos and the verb ponemos: nos ponemos.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Match each English phrase to the correct Spanish.
knowledgeCheck.explain: Colours come after the noun and agree with it (roja, blancas). Estos is for near, masculine plural things. Lleva goes with ella.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Read: “Hoy llevo una camisa de algodón azul. Los zapatos cuestan treinta euros.” How much do the shoes cost?

rubric.note: You are graded out of the total marks, shown as a percentage.
